name: אֲחִירַע
gloss: my brother is evil (?); or, my brother is a friend
summary: Ahira son of Enan was the prince of Naphtali in the wilderness: he stood with Moses at the numbering, camped with Naphtali north of the tabernacle, brought Naphtali’s offering on the twelfth day of the altar’s dedication, and led Naphtali’s host, last of the tribes in Dan’s camp, when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 10:27). The name is אֲחִי “brother of, my brother” with רַע, spelled as the word for “bad, evil”: “my brother is evil”, or “brother of evil”. That is a strange name to give, and the text does not explain it. It may instead be רֵעַ “friend, companion” (root רעה) in another vowelling, “my brother is a friend”; which root the second element belongs to is not certain.

evidence.note: Prince of the sons of Naphtali, in Dan’s camp on the north side.
His offering on the twelfth day; 7:83 “this was the offering of Ahira son of Enan”.
“Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali was אֲחִירַע בֶּן־עֵינָן.”
The element as the adjective רַע, “bad, evil”: the men of Sodom were רָעִים.
A name the text does explain from this root: Beriah, “because it was בְּרָעָה in his house”, given in a time of calamity.
The other possible element, רֵעַ “companion”: “a man of רֵעִים…, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother”.

note: Root key רעע for the element רַע as the text points it; the first element אֲחִי is the root אחה (entry ach). Enan (עֵינָן), his father, has no name entry yet. The reading “my brother is evil” is what the pointing gives, but it is an unlikely name; Beriah (1Ch 7:23) shows a child could be named for a time of רָעָה, and Ahira might be such a name, “brother of calamity”, though the text says nothing of his birth. The alternative from רֵעַ “friend” (root רעה, which has no entry yet) needs a vowel change; if the reviewer prefers it, the name should move to a רעה entry when one is written. The Septuagint’s Αχιρε transliterates and does not decide it.
